title: The pro-étale topos is replete
statement:
For every scheme $X$ and every inverse sequence $(F_n,t_n)$ of sheaves of sets on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with epimorphic transition maps, each projection
$p_m\colon\varprojlim_nF_n\to F_m$ is an epimorphism. Thus $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})$ is
replete in the sense of [det-pe-replete-definition].

proof.text: Fix a scheme $X$, an inverse sequence $(F_n,t_n)$ as in the statement, and $m\in\mathbf N$. Put $L=\varprojlim_n F_n$ and let $p_m:L\to F_m$ be the coordinate projection of [det-pe-replete-definition]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], it suffices, for every object $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $y\in F_m(U)$, to find a covering on which $y$ lifts to $L$. Fix such $U$ and $y$.

source.place: Tags 00WM (definition-sheaves-injective-surjective), part (2), and 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves); blueprint proof, first sentence

proof.text: Cover the arbitrary site object U by w-contractible affine objects, as in the covering clause of [det-pe-wcb-cover]. The adopted source proof obtains exactly this clause from ProEt.exists_isWContractibleRing_cover U: a covering sieve generated by maps from W_i, rings D_i, and isomorphisms W_i.left ≅ Spec D_i. Apply isWeaklyContractible_of_iso, carried by [lem-weil-pbc-source-affine-wcontractible-evaluation], to these isomorphisms. This gives weak contractibility in section universe max (u + 1) w, without restrictions on w or quasi-compactness of U. The stronger affine-open factorization of det-pe-wcb-cover is not needed here.

source.place: Proof, second and third sentences: the w-contractible affine covering and its weak contractibility; compare Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 4.2.8 and Stacks proetale.tex Tags 098I and 098H

proof.text: For every $i$, apply [det-pe-replete-on-contractible] to the original inverse sequence of sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and the weakly contractible object $W_i$ of step 2. Its hypotheses hold because all $t_n$ are epimorphisms by assumption. It gives surjectivity of $p_m(W_i):L(W_i)\to F_m(W_i)$. In particular there exists $x_i\in L(W_i)$ with $p_m(W_i)(x_i)=y|_{W_i}$. This is a lift in the limit of the original sequence, rather than a lift at only finitely many stages.

source.place: Proof, fourth sentence: apply the sectionwise sequential-limit lemma; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 3.2.3(1), proof

proof.text: The covering of step 2 and the lifts of step 3 show that every section $y\in F_m(U)$ is locally in the image of $p_m$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] makes $p_m$ an epimorphism. Since $m$ and the inverse sequence were arbitrary, [det-pe-replete-definition] now gives repleteness of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})$. The lifts on different covering members need no overlap compatibility: the required conclusion is local surjectivity, for which these separate lifts suffice.

source.place: Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves); Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.1.1 and Proposition 3.2.3(1), proof; blueprint proof, final sentence
